headline: Regulatory reckoning creates a 'perfect storm' for Australian fund managers as platforms slash investment options and due diligence intensifies post-Shield and First Guardian collapse
reasoning: Jon O'Keeffe describes a confluence of pressures on Australian fund managers: institutional clients are conducting deeper due diligence, regulators are pushing platforms to be more discerning, and platforms like Macquarie are publicly cutting the number of investment options on their menus. He characterises the Shield and First Guardian collapses as outright fraud and notes ASIC enforcement is at historically high levels with dozens of investigators deployed. He argues this creates a 'perfect storm' but sees a silver lining for managers with strong operations and governance, who will be better positioned to win large mandates from super funds and insurers.
quote: You know, these regulators are pushing platforms to be more discerning. You know, we've seen Macquarie come out publicly and say that they're going to slash the number of, um, you know, investment options available on their menu. And we're likely to see as these platforms move through these phases of due diligence on managers, more of those options being being cut. So is it just a really tough time to be an investment manager? Because not only do you have increasing regulation, but you've got AI encroaching on your patch... I think those who are doing it well, who have good operations, who can stand up to the scrutiny, will win. Like there's there's, you know, there's big, big mandates out there in in super and insurance land to be won.
episode_title: Fund managers face a regulatory reckoning
